findings.reason: the plan should extend one owner for git-layout resolution (or name that owner and justify the fork) instead of adding a parallel resolver, which is the recurring duplicate the rubric is about.
findings.text: `worktree_git_write_roots` resolves a worktree's own git directory and its repository's shared object store with `git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir --git-common-dir`, a git-layout resolution the repository already owns at least twice (`reckon/crew/node.py:repository_identity`, which collapses linked worktrees through `--git-common-dir`, and `reckon/worker_git_shim.py:_run_git_dir`); the plan proposes one more copy rather than extending an existing owner, so a change to how a worktree's git layout resolves would have to be made in four places.

findings.reason: each section that adds interface surface must account for it in its own text, per the one rule the interface_budget item enforces.
findings.text: the design adds an escape-hatch CLI option (`--no-fence REASON`), an installer CLI option (`--include-git-guard`) and a new MCP refusal family (`run_scoped_write`), against this week's public_definitions 1470, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23, and none of §1, §3 or §4 states what any of the added family members retires or merges, or why nothing can be.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — one composition point (`launch_plan` → `fence_argv` in reckon/_backends.py:3013) hides the whole mechanism behind a small interface: the protected set, its symlink/ancestry resolution, the worktree git write roots, the credential binds and the containment test are not visible to a caller, which names only the run's write roots and worktree.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan adds `worktree_git_write_roots` (reckon/_backends.py:2967), a fourth resolver of a checkout's git layout that shells `git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir --git-common-dir`, beside the owners that already resolve the same layout: `reckon/crew/node.py:repository_identity` (reckon/crew/node.py:1340, `--path-format=absolute --git-common-dir`) and `reckon/worker_git_shim.py:_run_git_dir` (reckon/worker_git_shim.py:594).
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1470, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; the sections add `--no-fence REASON` (reckon/cli.py:1826), `--include-git-guard` (reckon/cli.py:7419) and a `run_scoped_write` refusal family, and no design section names in its own text what any of them retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan searched the repository it extends and cites the mechanisms rather than the plan's account of them: bwrap (proved installed and unprivileged namespaces working), the existing per-dialect sandbox tiers (`sandbox_write_roots`/`delivery_write_roots`, which `fenced_write_roots` reuses — the plan's own record says "not a second list"), the `native_agent_guard.py` PreToolUse hook family the git guard sits beside, the existing worker shim PATH the git shim joins, and `read_run_pointer` for run scoping.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the two mechanisms that enforce one git rule (the PreToolUse `worker_git_guard.py` and the execution-time `worker_git_shim.py`) are each justified in the plan's own text: parsing a shell language cannot be made complete, so the shim resolves the repository at run time while the guard stays as the early, readable refusal. The fence itself is not a thin layer over the existing sandbox tier — the plan's premise is that the dialect sandbox is bypassed (`--dangerously-skip-permissions`, codex `worktree-full`), so the OS fence is the missing layer rather than a parallel one.
